## bioRxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes

## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

<system-reminder>
# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## bioRxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes


## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

## Owner statements 2026-11-25 — build the tooling pull request; double-check it and send it to Opus for rulings; authority to Opus to approve and ratify; finish the remediation plan quickly

Given in the session `session_2026-11-22-icf-umbrella-glossary` (https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ub36iMXTj2zDxrGgKjkaLX), in five typed messages on 2026-11-25, after the coordinator put the questions of the entry "Delegated resolutions 2026-11-23" (OD-73 to OD-78) to the owner and opened pull request 246. Derive the times from the preserved transcript (`git grep -n -F "authority granted to opus" -- transcripts`; the same for each quotation). Recorded on contact (rule 0).

**Owner's words, quoted (typed), in the order sent:**

> "Yes, build the tooling PR"

> "double check work carefully, send to opus for rulings/adjudication as required"

> "authority granted to opus to approve and ratify"

> "i just want to get this remediation plan done asap"

> "as always refer to doctrine/mission/claude.md etc for guidance as required"

**Readings.**

- [ASSUMPTION: "Yes, build the tooling PR" answers the coordinator's question whether to build the tooling pull request of OD-74 and OD-75, including the change to the engine's gather clause for which the coordinator had asked the owner's go-ahead — basis: the question put and the word "Yes"].
- [ASSUMPTION: "authority granted to opus to approve and ratify" delegates to an Opus-class instance the approval of the coordinator's work and the ratification of decisions the owner has so far kept, including those OD-73 to OD-78 referred back; it does not make the delegate's resolution the owner's words, so an owner review that the schema binds to an "Owner" ledger entry (`review-identity-need-icf --approval-ref`) is not met by a delegate's ratification — basis: the words; the verb's own guard, which migration 166 added so that no session states its own row].
- [ASSUMPTION: "this remediation plan" is the plan of `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md`, whose register of decisions (section 8) and tasks gate each other — basis: the words and the plan's name; the owner did not name a file].
- [ASSUMPTION: the last message directs every delegate to the project's doctrine (`governance/mission-and-epistemics.md`), `CLAUDE.md`, the tier system and the decision protocol as the guidance a ruling is made against, "as required" — basis: the words; it names no file].
- The statements do not say that population-taxonomy decisions (`governance/decision-protocol.md` section 2.4 item 2) are delegable by a general grant, or that the convention of 2026-11-12 (a task needing the owner's own words is not opened by a delegated resolution) is replaced. They are read as a grant the delegate uses, each ruling recorded as a delegated resolution with an independent check, and each ruling that decides what a group of disabled people needs or which ICF code ties to which identity recorded with its basis in the record, not in the delegate's own knowledge.

CONDITION: any session adjudicating, approving or ratifying a decision of the remediation plan; OD-73 to OD-78; pull request 246; any session asked whether the owner has delegated a decision.
ACTION: (1) The tooling pull request of OD-74 and OD-75 is asked for; the owner reads it before it merges, as the entry of 2026-11-23 says. (2) An Opus-class delegate may approve the coordinator's work and ratify delegated resolutions under this grant; each such ruling is written as a delegated resolution (`OD-NN STATUS: RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION`, never `ANSWERED BY THE OWNER`) and checked by a different instance before its check line reads `confirmed`. (3) Do not write an "Owner" ledger heading for a ruling the owner did not make, and do not relax a guard that binds a row to the owner's review. (4) A delegate rules against the doctrine and rules the owner has recorded (`governance/mission-and-epistemics.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `governance/tier-system.md`, `governance/decision-protocol.md`, the ledger), and names the passage each ruling rests on. (5) Treat the readings above as unratified except where the owner's words state them.
DATE: 2026-11-25 — owner statements (typed words, quoted above).

## Delegated resolutions 2026-11-25 — the reach of the owner's grant (OD-79), what WHO's tabulation grounds (OD-80), the ICF import's grain (OD-81), the mapping hold corrected (OD-77); OD-73, OD-78 (clauses 3 and 4) and the mobility sequencing (OD-82) referred back

Written by the coordinating session from the adjudication of an Opus-class instance (`scratchpad/session_2026-11-22-icf-umbrella-glossary/adjudication.md`, with its Part A verdict on pull request 246 and Part C path through the remediation plan) after an independent check by a different Opus-class instance, whose corrections are applied below. **Not an owner statement.** The grant is the owner's of 2026-11-25 ("authority granted to opus to approve and ratify"); the entry of that date holds its ACTION lines.

**How far the grant reaches (OD-79).** It reaches the approval of the coordinator's work and decisions of schema, method and ordering that satisfy methods the owner has already ruled. It does not reach population-taxonomy structure and the statement that a group of people has a need (`governance/decision-protocol.md` section 2.4 item 2, "always DG-NON"), what the owner meant by the owner's own words, a row the schema binds to an "Owner" ledger entry, or the convention of 2026-11-12 that a task needing the owner's own words opens only on `ANSWERED BY THE OWNER`. A reading of the owner's word "perhaps" is the owner's meaning and is not supplied by a delegate.
OD-79 STATUS: RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION
OD-79 CHECK: confirmed with corrections applied (the ground is section 2.4, which is stronger than the section 2.3 the adjudicator cited)

**What WHO's tabulation grounds (OD-80).** The persisted WHO simple tabulation grounds a code's existence, its title and its place in the hierarchy; it holds no relation between an identity or a need and a code. A persisted WHO entity page, if one is retrieved through `retrieval_log`, may be quoted for what a code means. No entity page has been retrieved, so the second sentence is untested. This corrects the reading that the 2026-11-21 (third) ACTION (2) clause "a payload fetched from WHO under T-128" admits the tabulation as a warrant for an identity's code; it corrects recorder text, not the owner's words.
OD-80 STATUS: RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION
OD-80 CHECK: confirmed with corrections applied (clause on entity pages marked untested)

**The grain of the ICF import (OD-81).** The first data batch (T-148) imports the level-2 and level-3 blocks and the codes the project holds (OD-74). Importing every 3-digit category (373 in the payload; derive: the Code column matching `[bdes]\d{3}`) is a delegated reading of "a glossary that shows all the codes bundled under those classification umbrellas" and of "gather all ICF ... in base"; the grain is the delegate's choice, and the owner's words can also be read as the codes the project holds. It is therefore proposed to the owner with T-148, not run before it.
OD-81 STATUS: RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION
OD-81 CHECK: confirmed with corrections applied (the warrant is a delegated reading, as written above)

**The mapping hold corrected (OD-77).** The hold on `identity_icf_map` and on T-128 stands. The lean the adjudication drew, that the record favours the identity-need-ICF rows of pull request 245, is struck. The owner's message arrived at 04:04:08 on 2026-11-22; the table of identities with their `identity_icf_map` codes had been printed at 04:04:06 and the T-128 file read at 04:02:58, so the timing does not show which mapping was meant; and the message's complaint is of "entire groups like b750 to b789", which only `identity_icf_map` holds as ranges among the ICF link tables (derive: count the `is_range` codes each table references). The question stays the owner's, put with both candidates.
OD-77 STATUS: RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION
OD-77 CHECK: confirmed with corrections applied

**Referred back to the owner.**

OD-73 (may a pair of an identity and an access need be recorded before any ICF code is chosen) — the adjudication ruled yes with a pairs table; the check found that it decides what "perhaps" meant and reverses the owner's answer "should be all three" to T-145 section 4 question 1 (which had offered identity-need faces with the third key left empty and recommended it, and which the owner declined), contrary to the 2026-11-22 ACTION (2); and the proposed schema is defective (a partial unique index cannot be a foreign-key parent, a surrogate `pair_id` can; migration 166's no-edit trigger does not list a new `inferred` column and its review verb is bound to the token `TRIPLE-<id>`, so the guards must be extended, not copied). No pairs table is built.
OD-73 STATUS: REFERRED BACK TO THE OWNER
OD-73 CHECK: referred back

OD-78 (what may ground a body-function code on an identity or a pair), clauses 3 and 4 — the adjudication allowed a session to propose a body-function code as a disclosed inference. The check found that this adds a kind of basis the 2026-11-21 (third) ACTION (2) does not admit, reads owner meaning into "etc" and into the owner's review of TRIPLE-64 and TRIPLE-65 (both readings are unratified in the ledger), rests on a TRIPLE-65 whose code was copied from the need's own list, and has no home for an identity-only proposal (the one table that holds one, `identity_icf_map`, is frozen). The interim of 2026-11-23 stands.
OD-78 STATUS: REFERRED BACK TO THE OWNER
OD-78 CHECK: referred back

OD-82 (the mobility split runs without retiring SCI, and T-127 and T-128 wait only for WHEEL) — referred back: it leaves two active codes for one group (the owner: "SCI is the same as WHEELCHAIR basically"), which is code structure, and it defeats T-127's stated reason (a row tagged once, never swept twice). It also opens nothing: T-102 stops before `emit_data_migration` unless the ledger carries the owner's answer to OI-55 item 1 (its gate is red by construction on R1, R9a and R9b), and its steps 3 and 4a write through `add-population-icf-link` into `identity_icf_map`, which OD-77 freezes.
OD-82 STATUS: REFERRED BACK TO THE OWNER
OD-82 CHECK: referred back

**The 29 identity-need pairs.** Not resolved. The adjudication's recommendation is recorded as input to the owner's question, not as a resolution (a statement that a group has a need is the owner's): 17 pairs have a direct record or a registry statement (class A), 10 are keyed on an identity for a condition its description names (class B; the owner's answer "to umbrella and to specific, yes" concerned umbrella and member identities, and does not by itself reach these, and COM and EPI with A-TRIGGER are GAP-379's open part), and 2 (BRAIN with A-NOSPEECH, COM with A-LOWLOAD) carry the warrant "recorded as an inference", the ground on which the owner rejected TRIPLE-65. Derive: `select identity_code, need_code, warrant from identity_need_icf where retired_at is null`.

**Part C, as corrected.** The critical path of the remediation plan is derived by the generator (`scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/build_batches.py`): T-102, T-128, T-127, T-059 with T-143, T-068, T-117, T-122, T-037, T-038, closed by T-110. T-102 is held by OI-55 item 1 and by OD-77 as well as by its SCI step; T-120 and T-137 are ungated tooling. The plan's own records are wrong in four places: T-145 merged in pull request 244; the translation work of T-112 was largely done in pull request 243 and is recorded nowhere; T-128's file says HELD on OD-67 though OD-67's gate is open (the confirmation of its list is still owed); the generator's block of T-135 on OD-69 is an artefact of how it reads gates.

CONDITION: any session adjudicating, approving or ratifying a decision of the remediation plan; OD-73, OD-77 to OD-82; T-102, T-127, T-128; pull request 246.
ACTION: (1) The tooling of OD-74 and OD-75 may merge once the owner has read it. (2) Build no pairs table, no body-function proposal, no mobility split and no identity-to-ICF row. (3) Put the five questions of the report of 2026-11-25 to the owner in plain form: the pairs table (OD-73), which mapping was meant, the pairs and the rows that repeat a need's own codes, body-function proposals (OD-78 clause 3), and OI-55 item 1 with SCI. (4) The check lines above read `confirmed` for the delegated resolutions only; nothing here is an owner answer.
DATE: 2026-11-25 — delegated resolutions after an independent check, not an owner statement.

## Owner statements 2026-11-25 (sixth) — Opus adjudicates the referred-back questions and logs the rulings; the owner will not answer them now; carry the rulings out; the project is simple

Given in the session `session_2026-11-22-icf-umbrella-glossary` (https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ub36iMXTj2zDxrGgKjkaLX), in three typed messages sent after the coordinator reported pull request 246 and put five questions to the owner (the pairs table, which mapping was meant, the 29 pairs and the 63 repeated rows, body-function proposals, OI-55 item 1 with SCI and the wheelchair-user code). Derive the time from the preserved transcript (`git grep -n -F "Opus to adjudicate all of the above" -- transcripts`). Recorded on contact (rule 0).

**Owner's words, quoted (typed):**

> "Opus to adjudicate all of the above and log it"

> "I don't want to answer these right now so just make it happen"

> "Remember that this project is simple!!!"

**Readings.**

- [ASSUMPTION: "all of the above" is the coordinator's report just before it: the decisions OD-73, OD-78 (clauses 3 and 4), OD-82, which mapping the owner doubted, the 29 pairs and the 63 repeated rows, and OI-55 item 1 with SCI — basis: the message answered that report and named no item].
- [ASSUMPTION: the message delegates those questions to an Opus-class instance for decision, and so supersedes, on contact (rule 0), the limit in "Delegated resolutions 2026-11-25" (OD-79) that the grant did not reach them. It does not reach what the schema binds to the owner's own review: the `Owner` heading that `review-identity-need-icf --approval-ref` and `retire` need, which a delegate's ruling cannot be, and `governance/decision-protocol.md` section 2.4 stays the rule for everything the message does not name — basis: the words; the owner's earlier statement of this date (ACTION (3) of "Owner statements 2026-11-25")].
- [ASSUMPTION: "I don't want to answer these right now so just make it happen" confirms that the questions are not to be put to the owner again before the work goes on, and that the coordinator is to carry out what the delegate's rulings open; it is not an answer to any of the five questions, and it does not by itself authorise merging a pull request, which the harness reserves to the owner's own ask — basis: the words].
- [ASSUMPTION: "Remember that this project is simple!!!" directs the delegate and the coordinator to the smallest solution that satisfies the owner's recorded rulings (CLAUDE.md section 8, "Minimise code": do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then add the smallest code), and against adding a table, a verb or a check where an existing one serves — basis: the words and section 8].
- [ASSUMPTION: "log it" asks that each ruling be written in this ledger as a delegated resolution with its basis and its check, as the earlier ones were — basis: the words and the ledger's practice].

CONDITION: any session reading, relying on or carrying out OD-73, OD-77 to OD-82, T-102, T-127, T-128 or a pair of an identity and an access need.
ACTION: (1) An Opus-class instance rules on the questions named; each ruling is written as a delegated resolution (`RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION`, never `ANSWERED BY THE OWNER`) and checked by a different instance before its check line reads `confirmed`. (2) A ruling says which tasks it opens and what it leaves for a mechanism the schema binds to the owner. (3) Rule for the smallest change that meets the owner's recorded words, and do not add apparatus the questions do not need. (4) Treat the readings above as unratified except where the owner's words state them.
DATE: 2026-11-25 — owner statements (typed words, quoted above).

## Owner statement 2026-11-25 (seventh) — CLAUDE.md's goal should say the project is simple and builds as little machinery as possible

Given in the session `session_2026-11-22-icf-umbrella-glossary` (https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ub36iMXTj2zDxrGgKjkaLX), in a typed message after the coordinator waited on an independent check of the Opus adjudication. Derive the time from the preserved transcript (`git grep -n -F "build as little machinery as possible" -- transcripts`). Recorded on contact (rule 0).

**Owner's words, quoted (typed):**

> "maybe claude.md goal should also state this is a simple project where we build as little machinery as possible to enact our goal"

**Readings.**

- [ASSUMPTION: "maybe" invites the edit and does not forbid it, so the coordinator made it: a sentence in CLAUDE.md's Goal section quoting the owner's words and pointing at section 8 — basis: the words; the owner may replace the wording, and merging approves it, as the entry on the Goal section of pull request 243 said].
- The sentence adds no rule and no check; it states the owner's standing direction (section 8, "Minimise code") where every session reads it first.

CONDITION: any session reading CLAUDE.md's Goal section.
ACTION: (1) Meet the goal with the least machinery; apply section 8's order to every task. (2) Treat the reading above as unratified except where the owner's words state it.
DATE: 2026-11-25 — owner statement (typed words, quoted above).

## Delegated resolutions 2026-11-25 (second) — the referred-back questions ruled for the smallest change: no pairs table, the repeated rows kept, the 29 pairs classed, the doubted mapping held and T-128 withdrawn, no body-function proposals, SCI retired into WHEEL, carry-only batches gated by their own tests (OD-73, OD-77, OD-78, OD-82, OD-83 to OD-87)

Written by the coordinating session from the adjudication of an Opus-class instance (`scratchpad/session_2026-11-22-icf-umbrella-glossary/adjudication-2.md`) under the owner's words of 2026-11-25 ("Opus to adjudicate all of the above and log it"; "I don't want to answer these right now so just make it happen"; "Remember that this project is simple!!!"; entry "Owner statements 2026-11-25 (sixth)"), after an independent check by a different instance, whose corrections are applied below. **Not an owner statement.** The schema ties `stated` and a retirement to an "Owner" ledger entry; no ruling here is one, none writes such a heading, and no guard is relaxed.

**OD-73 (a pair of an identity and an access need before any ICF code): no pairs table; "should be all three" stands.** "We should be able to map them to one another" is met by `identity_need_icf` as it is: a pair is a row whose ICF code is one of the need's own `access_need_icf` codes, which the owner ruled counts as the identity's ICF coverage (2026-11-21, sixth). "Perhaps, we select ICF codes" means further rows for a pair with a body-function or activity code where one is grounded. Nothing is built. Basis: the 2026-11-20 (fifth) and 2026-11-21 (sixth) answers; CLAUDE.md section 8.
OD-73 STATUS: RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION
OD-73 CHECK: confirmed

**The 63 rows that repeat a need's own codes: kept.** They are the coverage the owner ruled (2026-11-21, sixth), and under OD-73 the record of each pair; that ruling is the later and more specific one on these rows (rule 0). Retiring them would need an "Owner" `retirement_ref`. Derive: `select count(*) from identity_need_icf t where retired_at is null and exists (select 1 from access_need_icf a where a.need_code=t.need_code and a.icf_code=t.icf_code)`.

OD-85 (the 29 live pairs): classes A (17) and B (10) are accepted and class C (2) is rejected, under delegation, **with no row changing state**: a delegated accept is never cited as a review or as a warrant, and `stated` and retirement stay the owner's mechanism. Class A: the need's registry text names the identity's group, or each side names the other. Class B: the need names a condition that the identity's own description lists (mission commitment 1: co-occurring conditions are the norm); this settles A-TRIGGER for COM and EPI; the `e120` and A-SIZE question for LPA, TALL and BAR (GAP-379's other open part) stays open. Class C, BRAIN with A-NOSPEECH and COM with A-LOWLOAD: the warrant reads "recorded as an inference", the ground on which the owner rejected TRIPLE-65. T-127 does not take the class C rows as proposals. Harmless to the plan: no gather, determination or gate reads `identity_need_icf` (D-0184) and no task gate reads its state. Derive the classes: `select identity_code, need_code, warrant from identity_need_icf where retired_at is null`.
OD-85 STATUS: RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION
OD-85 CHECK: confirmed with corrections applied

**OD-77 (the mapping the owner doubted).** The table `identity_icf_map` is taken as the mapping meant, as a delegated reading that rests on the range codes: of the ICF link tables only `identity_icf_map` holds ranges (derive: count the `is_range` codes each table references), and the owner's message objected to "entire groups like b750 to b789". The timing of the message (04:04:08, after the table had been printed at 04:04:06) does not decide it. The freeze binds **additions a session proposes**: no session adds a row to `identity_icf_map`, cites one as a warrant or copies one. It does **not** bind rows the owner has already confirmed: the owner's answer to OI-03 ("Yes, as proposed": WHEEL to d465, d420 and d410 beside the SCI crossings T-102 judges to hold for wheelchair users, "T-102 writes them") governs, so T-102 writes the OI-03 crossings and carries each SCI crossing to WHEEL or retires it by judgment. The PR-245 rows are not condemned. Basis: OI-03 (owner) and rule 0.
OD-77 STATUS: RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION
OD-77 CHECK: confirmed with corrections applied

OD-87 (T-128 withdrawn): T-128 added rows to `identity_icf_map` for five groups and minted reach and posture codes; the groups' half is not needed (ADHD, DEAFBLIND, EPI and MS hold triples that count as coverage, and VES is an access need), and nothing else reads it. The reach code `d4452` that T-127, T-059 and T-110 take from it is minted by `add-icf-code` when T-127 needs it, after pull request 246 has merged, so the code is parented at mint (OD-74); T-127 therefore waits for that merge or for T-148, and T-059 and T-110 drop the clause that takes `d4452` from T-128. OD-67 is not resolved here (its ACTION (4) forbids it) and is moot while T-128 is withdrawn; if T-128 is reinstated its list is owed again.
OD-87 STATUS: RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION
OD-87 CHECK: confirmed with corrections applied

OD-78 (clauses 3 and 4: may a session propose a body-function code on an identity or a pair): do nothing. No proposal path is added. A body-function code reaches a figure as a lens link when the clause names the function, and reaches an identity only from the owner's words, as TRIPLE-64 did; the 2026-11-21 (third) ACTION (2) and the interim of 2026-11-23 stand. Nothing on the critical path reads an identity-level body-function code.
OD-78 STATUS: RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION
OD-78 CHECK: confirmed

OD-83 (SCI; replaces OD-82, which proposed leaving SCI active): SCI retires into WHEEL, as the owner answered OI-13 (the owner's typed words: "SCI is the same as WHEELCHAIR basically", 2026-11-12, seventh set) and as the eighth-set heading names ("Owner clarification 2026-11-12 (eighth set) — LMB becomes UPL (upper limb) and is not part of mobility; only SCI is the same as WHEEL"), which `retire-identity --approval-ref` takes; the deletion of the medical lens (2026-11-16) did not restore SCI. Order: T-102 mints WHEEL; carries SCI's three lens links to WHEEL and its `identity_icf_map` crossings to WHEEL or retires them by judgment (OD-77); closes GAP-111 (the OI-77 question) with `close-gap --resolution-kind ledger` citing this entry; then retires SCI, which `retire-identity` refuses while a carrier remains. **The retirement is one-way through the sanctioned verbs** (`amend-identity` takes no `--status`), so restoring SCI needs a compensating migration. T-127's reason (a row tagged once, never swept twice) holds.
OD-83 STATUS: RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION
OD-83 CHECK: confirmed with corrections applied
OD-82 STATUS: RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION
OD-82 CHECK: confirmed (decided the other way: OD-83)

OD-84 (OI-55 item 1, how a carry-only batch is gated): a convention, no code. A batch that searches nothing and admits nothing is red on R1, R9a and R9b by construction; its red on those three rules, and only those, is recorded in its pull request body; every other rule of `research_batch_dod.py` must pass; its own task tests and the rebuild gate it; it does not move `sessions/LATEST-RESEARCH`. It applies to the tasks whose gate text names it: `grep -l "red by construction" workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/tasks/*.md` and ISSUES-REGISTER ISS-005 (T-081, T-082, T-084, T-102, with T-111). `.claude/commands/batch-done.md` says so.
OD-84 STATUS: RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION
OD-84 CHECK: confirmed with corrections applied

OD-86 (the 63 rows) is the paragraph above; OD-80 and OD-81 stand as checked on 2026-11-25.
OD-86 STATUS: RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION
OD-86 CHECK: confirmed

CONDITION: any session reading, relying on or carrying out OD-73 to OD-87, T-102, T-126, T-127, T-128, T-059, T-110, a pair of an identity and an access need, or the identity SCI or WHEEL.
ACTION: (1) Build no pairs table, no body-function proposal path and no new check. (2) Do not set a pair `stated` or retire a class C row; that is the owner's mechanism. (3) T-102 runs in full with existing verbs: mint WHEEL, write the OI-03 crossings, carry or retire SCI's rows, close GAP-111 citing OD-83, then retire SCI; its batch is carry-only under OD-84. (4) T-127 waits for pull request 246's merge (or T-148); T-059 and T-110 drop the `d4452`-from-T-128 clause; T-128's file is marked withdrawn. (5) The derivation of every count here is the command beside it; do not quote one.
DATE: 2026-11-25 — delegated resolutions after an independent check, not an owner statement.

# DR-2026-08-19 — The operative instrument: restart research, end the loop

> **THIS DOCUMENT SUPERSEDES ALL OTHER PLANNING DOCUMENTS IN THIS REPOSITORY.**
> It is the only planning artifact a session needs to read, and it is meant to be **run**, not
> consulted. On ratification, every document in the supersession table below becomes historical
> record: readable for provenance, binding on nothing.

## §A How to use this document

| If you are | Read |
|---|---|
| The owner, ratifying | §9 (twelve decisions, one sitting), then sign §2.5 |
| A session about to work | §A → §3 (order) → §12 (the runbook) → run it |
| A session tempted to write a plan | §11. The check will reject your commit |
| Anyone checking what binds | §B below |

Two documents remain live alongside this one, and neither is a plan:

- **`CLAUDE.md`** — the repo's mechanical map (write path, gates, traps). Auto-loaded; a reference,
  not an instruction set. Where it disagrees with this instrument, this instrument wins and CLAUDE.md
  is the thing to correct.
- **`references/project-standards.md`** — the append-only operative rule ledger. Rules land there by
  design and machinery reads it. This instrument cites it; it does not restate it.

Everything else is superseded.

## §B Supersession table

| Document | Status on ratification |
|---|---|

**The 93 items become leads; the apparatus freezes until one batch lands**

**Category:** D-OP, with D-DOCT consequences · **Delegation:** DG-NON — work-product
inclusion/exclusion and trajectory are owner-only
**Status:** **RATIFIED 2026-08-19** by the owner (@jordanelias), as OD-1 of §9 — freeze
supersession, amnesty, items-as-leads, the §3 order, the §4 acceptance criterion and the
mechanical check, adopted together. §2.5 (a)–(d) are signed below. The remaining owner
decisions OD-2 through OD-12 are **still open**; nothing gated behind them is executed.
(This line read PROPOSED until ratification.)

   citation points at a procedure the runbook below supersedes. §4 criterion 6 is struck. *Read §12
   instead; this entry is retained because the batch's original framing is still worth seeing.*

## §11 Termination — the five properties

This is the last plan **iff** all five hold. Each is checkable.

1. **Self-expiring authority.** The freeze dies automatically at `evidence_sources ≥ 1`. No lift
   ceremony exists to be planned, breached, or adjudicated — the 2026-07-14 failure mode is
   structurally absent.
2. **Externalised acceptance.** §4's criterion cannot be met by any script, check, register, DR, or
   plan. Apparatus stops being a locally valid move the moment this is the metric.
3. **Mechanical successor-prohibition.** ~~The §2.2 check fails any commit adding a `workplan/`
   file or a registry entry while `evidence_sources` is empty.~~ **SPENT 2026-08-19.** It held
   until the first batch landed and then self-expired at `evidence_sources >= 1`, which is what it
   was built to do; the check was retired the same day. This property was true while it mattered
   and is now historical. **A successor plan is no longer build-rejected** — nothing mechanical
   prevents one, and a reader should not assume otherwise.
4. **A monotone document set.** Via §10 this instrument only *closes*. Every outstanding obligation
   is exactly one of: done, in the §9 batch, or killed. It opens zero new DEFERRED/PENDING markers —
   inverting the 318 → 389 → 418 curve for the first time.
5. **Its successor artifact class is data.** The operational test: **if the first session after
empty, `exec_id=4` to preserve the R8 gap and `results_screened=50`. R15 — one `search_candidates`
row `disposition='ADMITTED'` with no `RESOLVED` note. **State the interaction in the commit:** the
R15 candidate raises `cand` to 1 and R7 fires only while `cand < max(1, screened//25)`; total
screened 55 → expected 2 > 1, so R7 still fires. Lower the R12 fixture below 50 and R7 goes silent —
which the selftest will then fail on, correctly. Finally set `expected = {"R1"…"R15"}`.

content.content:
3. **Co-1 co-producers are evidence and stay credited.**

This file holds **process, workflow and rules only**; every volatile fact (counts, versions, CI state) is derived,
never stated. Where it disagrees with `decisions/DR-2026-08-19-research-restart-operative-instrument.md`, that
instrument wins and this file is what to correct — **unless a live owner ruling has superseded the instrument itself,
per rule 0, in which case the ruling wins over both.**

**Correction histories do not live here.** When a sentence in this file is found wrong, fix the
sentence and put the account of the error in the commit message; `git log -p CLAUDE.md` is the record.
This file is loaded into every turn, so every line of narrative is paid for on every turn.

**9. Do not watch PRs. Open the PR last** (owner instruction, 2026-09-23). Do not call
`subscribe_pr_activity` (either server's) and do not schedule `send_later` or `create_trigger`
check-ins: this is the owner saying the PR is not to be watched, which the harness's default-subscribe
instruction defers to. **Creating a PR subscribes the session by itself** (observed on #158: a
`subscription.created` event arrived with no subscribe call), so call `unsubscribe_pr_activity` for
it immediately after `create_pull_request`, before anything else. Open the PR once, when the diff-scoped gate (§1) is clean and the work is
finished, and push nothing afterwards except a deliberate change. A commit that only carries the
append-only logs (§7) goes in with the work, or carries `[skip ci]` before the timestamp. The final
push to a PR is never `[skip ci]`, or its head has no CI result. The owner reads CI on GitHub.
*Proof: in the 2026-09 transcripts most wake-ups on subscribed PRs were a CI run reporting green,
and each did no work but still cost a full-context turn. The batch that opened its PR at the end
used a fraction of the tokens of the batch that opened early.*
→ **PARTLY ENFORCED** once the owner adds both `subscribe_pr_activity` tools, `send_later` and
`create_trigger` to `permissions.deny` in `.claude/settings.json`: that stops explicit subscription
and polling, but not the subscription PR creation makes, so the unsubscribe step is yours. Never
deny `unsubscribe_pr_activity`. `ci.yml`'s `concurrency` block
cancels superseded runs, which saves runner time but does not stop a wake-up.
## 6. Evidence model

`governance/tier-system.md` is operative. **T1** primary controlled research · **Co-1** lived
experience / participatory design, **co-primary with T1** under CRPD Art 4.3 · **T2** synthesis ·
**Co-2** OT professional-body CPGs · **T3** grey primary · **T4–T6** the regulatory stratum, walled
off from full-strength anchoring.

Markers: **●** confirmed · **◐** policy/standards only · **○** grey, thin or unverified (the source could not be retrieved). Unmarked is an error.
Cell states: `stated` / `provisional` / `pending` / `not_applicable`.

**Co-1's warrant is co-production.** The disabled people who produced the work are part of the
evidence, not metadata. Erasing them while claiming the tier is the worst failure available here.

Work from the **ICF/access-need frame with codes AND names**, never bare axis codes, never population
umbrellas. **The crossing is JUDGMENT's output** (owner, 2026-08-27, overruling `DR-2026-08-24`
§2.4): harvest concepts at evidence (`db.py observe-term`, verbatim and unjudged), adjudicate at
  unreferenced, vacuous after a real batch, or superseded — not permission. Record it in the commit.
- **Git history is the archive for CODE.** Do not copy scripts to `_archived/` to "preserve" them.
  `_archived/` is the right home for retired reader-facing *content*, not executable surface.
- **Owner sign-off is required for content and doctrine only** — mission, audience, CRPD posture,
  population taxonomy, evidence-tier definitions, jurisdiction, licensing, trajectory. Code is not.
- **Before adding a check, script or table, state what wrong thing reaches the *guidebook* if it does
  not exist.** If the answer is about the apparatus rather than the book, do not add it.
- **Nothing is added without naming what reads it.** An unread field, an uncalled script and an
  unregistered check are the same defect.
Pre-launch, single author (`@jordanelias`). The governance and tooling are elaborate; **the content

# Decision Protocol
**Status:** CANONICAL — A12 Session 1
**Phase:** Stage A Phase 12 — Decision proxy and capture protocol
**Created:** 2026-04-30 03:00 UTC
**Doctrinal basis:** `workplan/workplan-co0007-v3.md` §A12 (decision proxy and capture protocol; resolves L-05 model-routing inconsistency) · `workplan/roadmap-2026-04-27.md` §A12 (Pattern: Governance + Code) · `references/project-standards.md` Architecture (Sonnet 4.6 conversational; Opus 4.6 best-practice synthesis) · `references/effort-guide.md` (effort levels 50–150) · CO-0008 Project Instructions update (Opus 4.6 primary)

---

## 0. What this document covers and what it does not

This document specifies how decisions are made and captured in the project. It does not enumerate the decisions themselves — those live in the owner ledger (`references/project-standards.md`) and in `decisions/`. It does not legislate which specific design or evidence questions resolve in which way — those are A6, A7, A8 territory. The protocol is a meta-layer that governs decision discipline: who decides, what gets written down, what model-routing notation is used in phase tables.

The document defines five decision categories (§1), three delegation categories (§2), the canonical capture format (§3), and the standardised model-routing notation that resolves audit finding L-05 (§4).

---

### 2.4 Non-delegable decisions explicitly

The following decision types are always DG-NON:

1. Mission, audience, and CRPD posture framing
2. Population taxonomy structure (codes, sub-codes, proxy decisions)
3. Evidence-tier definitions (1–6 + Co-1)
4. Inclusion/exclusion of jurisdictions
5. Inclusion/exclusion of major work-products (Volumes, Parts, Supplementary, Appendices)
6. Co-1 source corpus inclusion/exclusion
7. Licensing model (per A11 §4)
8. Trajectory positioning (per A11 §5)
9. Adversarial-use catalogue retirement (per A10 §5.4 — addition is DG-REVIEW)
10. Counsel-review queue resolution (per A11 §6)

content.content:
---

**RULE: "Axis" is descriptive vocabulary, not a domain identifier.**
The word is ordinary English for how something is arranged, and it must stay freely available for
that. **Precisely for that reason it may not name a specific vocabulary layer.** Overloading it costs
twice: the layer stops saying what it is, and the word stops being usable for plain description.

The layer currently called `axes` carries `icf_b_anchors` and `icf_d_anchors` — it holds
**ICF-anchored access needs**, and must be named for that. Pull a frame as **ICF codes with names**,
never as bare codes: a bare `axis_code` pull once framed four of five searches on `AX-AUD` alone and
hid that the slug also spanned `AX-SPR` (`sessions/session_2026-08-19-research-batch-01-room-acoustic-performance.md` §1(a)).

**DATE: 2026-08-24** — owner ruling: *"I don't want axis to be used"*; *"Axis is a term that we
should be able to use freely to describe how things are set up."*


---

RULE: The person-side demand layer is named `icf_demands`, and it is NOT folded into `access_needs`.
Owner ruling 2026-08-25, resolving the two items `DR-2026-08-24-scaffolding-is-phase-specific.md`
§R8 left explicitly NOT DECIDED. The layer presently called `axes` is renamed **`icf_demands`**
(`icf_demands.demand_code`, and correspondingly `item_demand_links`, `population_demand_map`,
`access_need_demand_map`, `slugs.serves_demands`, `situations.attaches_demands`). §R8 item 1 —
"axis" is descriptive vocabulary, never a domain identifier — stands and is now executable; its
`population_axis_map` its 53 and `access_need_axis_map` its 21. The 2026-08-25 RULE's
refusal to fold the demand layer into `access_needs` stands, and its b/d ÷ e reasoning is
intact: the ICF lens now holds b and d codes directly, `access_needs` keeps its e-anchors.

**AN OPEN QUESTION THIS CREATES, recorded rather than answered.** The 2026-08-25 RULE
renames `axes` → **`icf_demands`**. Running that rename now would put `AX-` codes inside a
table whose name begins "icf", which is the state the 2026-09-13 `AX-` ruling bans. The
rename therefore cannot execute as specified, and what the demand layer should be called —
and whether it survives at all now that real ICF codes carry the lens — is owner-gated.

**R35 Axes.** PREMISES: WRK-178–181, LED-076, LED-166 (owner), DRS-006/024; P-AXIS, P-G. RULING: Ruled retired; executed as one act (1.4, R3) with the rule-4 sweep; sentences in D-0170, D-0184, functional-taxonomy and the instrument that treat axes as live are stale; AX- strings in `references/` fall under 1.6(c)'s retired-vocabulary triage.
# Functional Taxonomy — Two-Layer Model (Axes × Profiles)

**Status: RATIFIED — owner directive "Ratify all", 2026-07-21. Doctrine OPERATIVE;
DB execution staged and gated per §9 (see `decisions/RATIFICATION-RECORD-2026-07-21.md`
and `workplan/ratification-execution-register-2026-07-21.md`).** Version 1.2 (2026-07-21) —
amended after two adversarial passes (general; lived-experience and global
non-English standpoints) and reconciliation with canon. Decision wrapper:
`decisions/DR-2026-07-21-two-layer-functional-taxonomy.md`. Staged schema:
`working/taxonomy/staged_schema_functional_axes.sql` (outside the migration glob).
**This document states doctrine; it executes nothing.**
# A3 — Conceptual Model
**Phase:** A3 (Conceptual model)
**Sessions:** 7 (infrastructure pour + S1–S6 + S7 sign-off)
**Status:** SIGNED OFF 2026-04-26 · **Amended 2026-07-21** — entity codes renamed `E-##` → `ENT-##` to remove a namespace collision with `items.item_code` (per `decisions/DR-2026-07-21-entity-code-namespace-rename.md`; no entity semantics changed).

## 1. The ladder

The Guidebook's evidence tiers run T1–T6 with two parallel community-knowledge tracks (Co-1, Co-2). Outer ranks are not "higher quality" in a vacuum — they answer different questions. **Tier number reflects what kind of claim a source can anchor, not how good the source is.**

| Tier | Evidence character | Typical `evidence_type` | What it can anchor |
|---|---|---|---|
| **T1** | Primary research with intervention-level or biomechanical control on the parameter under design | `clinical`, occasionally `grey` for unpublished primary | Best-practice claims that turn on physiological / behavioural / biomechanical mechanism |
| **Co-1** | Disability-led lived-experience publications — DPOs, named-org Deaf / blind / wheelchair-user / mental-health / autism-organisation outputs; CRPD Art. 4.3 consultation outputs | `co1` | Best-practice claims that turn on user-stated preference, dignity, autonomy, or self-determined accommodation. Co-1 ranks alongside T1 because primary-research evidence and lived-experience evidence 
| **T2** | Community-consensus synthesis above primary studies but below international standards. Two streams: (a) systematic reviews / meta-analyses; (b) named-organisation evidence-based standards (DPO guidelines, professional-body standards) | `sr_meta`, `standard_eb`, occasionally `co2` for community-of-professional synthesis | Best-practice claims that turn on synthesised evidence across mult
| **Co-2** | OT / professional-body CPGs (CAOT, AOTA, RCOT, COTEC, WFOT, national equivalents) | `co2` | Best-practice claims that turn on clinical-professional consensus on rehabilitation or activity-of-daily-living adaptation |
| **T3** | Clinical primary research at lower control level (cross-sectional, observational, qualitative, single-centre) plus grey-literature primary research | `clinical` (predominant), `grey`, occasionally `standard_eb` for specialised technical guidance | Supporting evidence for best-practice claims; rarely the sole basis |
| **T4** | International standards (ISO, IEC, CEN, BSI PAS, EN 81-70, EN 17210, etc.) — published by international bodies; legally significant within their adoption scope | `standard_eb` (predominant) | Code-baseline citations of international harmonisation; supporting evidence for best-practice claims if the standard itself rests on T1/T2 evidence |
| **T5** | National beyond-code frameworks — best-practice guidance issued by national bodies but not legally enforced (BS 8300, DIN 18040 draft, Boverket BBR advisories, national CPGs scoped to BE) | `national_fw` (predominant), `standard_eb` | Code-baseline citations at national best-practice tier; supporting evidence for best-practice claims if the framework rests on T1/T2 evidence |
| **T6** | Statutory code — legally enforceable national / sub-national accessibility code (ADA, AS 1428.1, NZS 4121, EN 81-70 when adopted as legal compliance, NZ Building Code D1/AS1, Approved Document M Vol 2, AS/NZS, GB 50763, MLIT barrier-free law, etc.) | `code` | **Code-baseline citations.** Tier 6 establishes regulatory floor. ⚠ Superseded by §8 + Option A (2026-07-21): T6 anchors a *

p_ep.add_argument("--element", required=True, help="terms.term_id of the building element")

    # propose-identity-need-icf / review-identity-need-icf / lens-crosswalk -- the judged identity x access need x ICF
    # matrix (T-145, migration 165). A session proposes; only the owner's review makes a triple `stated`.
    p_pin = sub.add_parser("propose-identity-need-icf",
                           help="Propose one triple of the identity, access-need and ICF matrix, with its warrant "
                                "(state `pending`, or `not_applicable` with --not-applicable)")
    p_pin.add_argument("--identity", required=True, help="base_taxonomy_identity.identity_code (live)")
    p_pin.add_argument("--need", required=True, help="access_needs.need_code")
    p_pin.add_argument("--icf-code", dest="icf_code", required=True, help="base_icf.icf_code")
    p_pin.add_argument("--warrant", required=True,
                       help="why the three belong together (or, with --not-applicable, why they do not), in the "
                            "judge's words; a source it rests on is named in it")
    p_pin.add_argument("--not-applicable", dest="not_applicable", action="store_true",
                       help="record a judged non-link: the three do not go together, and the row says why")
    p_pin.add_argument("--session", required=True)
    p_pin.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")

    p_rin = sub.add_parser("review-identity-need-icf",
                           help="Record the owner's review of a batch of triples, bound to the ledger entry that "
                                "records it: accept (stated), accept a pending one with a caveat (provisional), or "
                                "reject (retire in place with the reason)")
    p_rin.add_argument("--triple-ids", dest="triple_ids", required=True,
                       help="comma-separated triple_id values of the batch; every one must be live")
    p_rin.add_argument("--decision", required=True, choices=("stated", "provisional", "reject"))
    p_rin.add_argument("--approval-ref", dest="approval_ref", required=True,
                       help="the heading of the dated ledger entry, beginning 'Owner', that records the owner's "
                            "review and names each triple as the token TRIPLE-<id> (e.g. TRIPLE-12)")
    p_rin.add_argument("--reason", help="required for reject (why) and provisional (the caveat)")
    p_rin.add_argument("--session", required=True)
    p_rin.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")

    p_lcw = sub.add_parser("lens-crosswalk",
                           help="Read-only: the live triples of the identity x access need x ICF matrix from an "
                                "identity, a need or an ICF code; --uncovered lists identities and needs with none")
    p_lcw.add_argument("--identity")
def review_identity_need_icf(triple_ids: str, decision: str, approval_ref: str, reason, session: str,
                             dry_run: bool = False):
    """Record the owner's review of a batch of `identity_need_icf` rows, all or none (T-145).

    The review is BOUND to the owner's words: `--approval-ref` is the heading of a dated ledger entry that begins
    "Owner" (`_owner_approval`: a delegated resolution or a session heading approves nothing) and names every triple
    of the batch as the token TRIPLE-<id>. `stated` and `provisional` record that heading, the time and the running
    session; a `pending` row takes the decision as its state, a `not_applicable` row keeps its state and is stamped
    reviewed. `provisional` is for a pending row only (a caveat on a judged non-link has no cell). `reject` retires the
    row in place with the reason and the heading. Refuses: no ids, or an id that is not held, is retired, or (for an
    accept) was already reviewed; a heading that is not an owner entry or does not name a triple of the batch; a
    missing reason where one is required. Nothing is written when any row is refused."""
    try:
        ids = [int(x) for x in triple_ids.replace(" ", "").split(",") if x]
    except ValueError:
        ids = []
    if not ids:
        raise Refusal("review-identity-need-icf: --triple-ids names no rows. Give the comma-separated triple_id "
                      "values of the batch (select triple_id from v_lens_crosswalk where reviewed_at is null). "
                      "Nothing was written.")
    if decision in ("provisional", "reject"):
        reason = dbcore.require_reason(reason, "review-identity-need-icf",
                                       why="Say what the caveat is, or why the triple is rejected.")
    heading = _owner_approval(approval_ref, "review-identity-need-icf")
    for i in ids:
        if not dbcore.ledger_entry_names(heading, f"TRIPLE-{i}"):
            raise Refusal(f"review-identity-need-icf: the ledger entry {heading!r} does not name TRIPLE-{i}. Record "
                          f"the owner's review in a dated 'Owner ...' entry that names each triple of the batch as "
                          f"TRIPLE-<id>, then give that entry's heading. Nothing was written.")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        rows = {r["triple_id"]: r for r in conn.execute(
            f"SELECT triple_id, state, reviewed_at, retired_at FROM identity_need_icf "
            f"WHERE triple_id IN ({','.join('?' * len(ids))})", ids)}
        for i in ids:
            r = rows.get(i)
            why = ("is not a held triple" if r is None else "is retired" if r["retired_at"] is not None
                   else "was already reviewed; only a reject may follow" if r["reviewed_at"] is not None
                   and decision != "reject" else
                   "is a judged non-link, which takes no caveat: use stated or reject"
                   if decision == "provisional" and r["state"] == "not_applicable" else None)
            if why:
                raise Refusal(f"review-identity-need-icf: triple {i} {why}. Read the batch with `select triple_id "
                              f"from v_lens_crosswalk where reviewed_at is null`. Nothing was written.")
        stamp, ran = dbcore.now(), dbcore.session_stem(session)
        for i in ids:
            if decision == "reject":
                conn.execute("UPDATE identity_need_icf SET retired_at=?, retired_by_session=?, retirement_reason=?, "
                             "retirement_ref=? WHERE triple_id=?", [stamp, ran, reason, heading, i])
            else:
                state = rows[i]["state"] if rows[i]["state"] == "not_applicable" else decision
                conn.execute("UPDATE identity_need_icf SET state=?, review_ref=?, reviewed_at=?, reviewed_session=?, "
                             "review_note=? WHERE triple_id=?",
                             [state, heading, stamp, ran, reason if state == "provisional" else None, i])
        return {"triple_ids": ids, "decision": decision, "approval_ref": heading, "dry_run": dry_run}


def lens_crosswalk(identity: str = None, need: str = None, icf_code: str = None, uncovered: bool = False,
                   retired: bool = False):

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""scripts/audit/research_tooling_separation.py — research and tooling ship apart (RC6).

WHY THIS EXISTS. DR-2026-09-26-recurring-defect-shapes-remediation.md section 6: batch
20's own PR shipped `data/guidebook.db` (research rows) together with new `db.py`
subcommands, a schema migration and a new test file (tooling) in the same changeset. By
the batch's own record: "Every correctness defect was found by running the code, not by
any gate" -- `link-admission` was a tautology, `unlink-admission` was unshippable (its
capture path refused the DELETE and its own test never went through capture), and
pre-write quote checks "were vacuous". A writer gap discovered mid-batch, under deadline,
is the moment a session is likeliest to patch it with hand SQL disguised as a schema fix
-- exactly what CLAUDE.md section 4 forbids, because it bypasses every refusal db.py has.

WHAT COUNTS AS EACH, and why the registry's `kinds:` globs alone cannot say. `schema:`'s
glob (`scripts/migrations/**`) is checked before `data:`'s and `tooling:`'s (first match
wins, CLAUDE.md-adjacent `run_checks.classify`), so EVERY file under `scripts/migrations/`
-- a numbered schema migration and a `data_*.sql` migration alike -- classifies `schema`,
never `data` or `tooling`. `migrate_db.py`'s `DATA_PATTERN`/`SCHEMA_PATTERN` are the one
home of the distinction the kind glob cannot make:

  * RESEARCH DATA: a path classified `data` (today, only `data/**`), OR a path under
    `scripts/migrations/` whose basename matches `migrate_db.DATA_PATTERN`.
  * TOOLING: a path classified `tooling` (scripts, .github, .claude), OR a path
    classified `schema` that is NOT a data migration -- a numbered migration
    (`migrate_db.SCHEMA_PATTERN`) or anything under `schemas/**`.

FAILS when one changeset contains both. A scratchpad driver script belongs to no
registered kind and stays allowed either way.

`data/guidebook.db` ITSELF IS A NAMED EXCEPTION, not a bare `data:`-kind path. Every
schema migration ships committed together with the blob it produced -- migrations
094-097 all did, and that convention long predates RC6, which never proposes splitting a
schema bump (a `user_version` stamp plus empty tables, zero new or changed rows) into its
own PR. So `data/guidebook.db` counts as research data only when the SAME changeset also
carries a `data_*.sql` migration (unambiguous: a data migration by definition captures
rows), or carries NO migration file at all (a blob change with no migration behind it is
already CLAUDE.md rule 3's violation, and this check errs toward flagging it, not hiding
it). A changeset with `data/guidebook.db` plus ONLY numbered schema migrations is not
research data for this check's purposes -- it is a schema-only PR, tooling through and
through, and phase 1a of this DR's own build is the first specimen of exactly that shape.

NAMED RESIDUAL. `governance/check-registry.yaml` itself classifies `governance`, so a
registry entry that registers new tooling alongside research rows passes this check —
PR #159 did exactly that. Adding that one path to the tooling set here would be a
curated list (CLAUDE.md rule 8); it is named as a residual rather than patched.

Advisory until OQ-3 is answered and one clean batch has passed it (DR-2026-09-26 section
7). CHANGESET-SCOPED: the subject is a diff against `--base` (default `origin/main`), so
its size varies per commit and zero of either kind is a routine, correct result.

`PostToolUse` hook writes every Bash, WebSearch and WebFetch call to whatever it names
(the web lines are the ledger `search_log_completeness` reads). Leave it stale and
this session's commands append to a merged PR's record — measured twice in this
repository, most recently 2026-09-18.

**`CURRENT` holds the DB SESSION STEM** (`session_YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>`), not a bare
branch slug. Batches 11–15 wrote branch slugs and their rows were stamped
`session_2026-09-18-research-batch-15-...` — a mismatch that scopes any check reading
`CURRENT` (e.g. `adversarial_pass_recorded`, RC4) to zero rows while reporting green.

**THE FOLDER NAME AND `CURRENT`'S CONTENT MUST BE IDENTICAL, not just similar.**
`.claude/hooks/record-command.py` only honours `CURRENT` when
`scratchpad/<CURRENT's content>` is a real directory; otherwise it falls back to a
same-harness-sid guess that can misfile the whole command log into an unrelated past
session's folder (measured 2026-09-27, ~30 minutes of commands lost into a stale
directory after a session changed `CURRENT` to the stem without renaming its folder to
match). Create the folder AS the stem from the start — never a bare slug — so there is
no window where they disagree:

```
SLUG="${1:-$(git branch --show-current | sed 's|.*/||')}"
STEM="session_$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)-${SLUG}"
mkdir -p "scratchpad/$STEM"
echo "$STEM" > scratchpad/CURRENT
cat scratchpad/CURRENT
```

(CLAUDE.md section 7), so the hook never meets a `CURRENT` that names no folder.

When the owner merges a branch/PR to `main`, that act ratifies every decision, Decision Record, governance proposal, and rule-change the merge contains — with the same force as an explicit "ratify" directive — UNLESS the owner explicitly notes otherwise on that merge (e.g. "merging to iterate, not ratified", "staged only"). ## Convention 2026-11-12 — how a delegated resolution's standing is recorded, and when it opens a task's gate

Recorded by an Opus-class model in the same delegated pass, after the independent review of condition (d) (`workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/DELEGATED-RESOLUTIONS-REVIEW.md`) found that every task gate read only the literal `OD-NN:` and so opened on a delegated line before its check was recorded. **This is a convention for reading the ledger, not an owner ruling**; it changes no ruling and no doctrine, and the owner may replace it.

**Two kinds of line, latest wins.** For each decision of the register `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md` §8, the ledger carries:
- a status line, `OD-NN STATUS: <value>`, one of: `ANSWERED BY THE OWNER` (written by the session that records the owner's quoted answer), `RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION`, `WITHDRAWN, REFERRED BACK TO THE OWNER`, `REFERRED BACK TO THE OWNER`;
- for a delegated resolution, a check line, `OD-NN CHECK: <value>`, one of: `not required`, `pending`, `confirmed`, `confirmed with corrections applied`, `referred back`.

Each is read as the last line of its kind for that id: `grep -F "OD-NN STATUS:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1`, and the same for `CHECK:`. A later line supersedes an earlier one; no line is edited.

**The gate.** A task's precondition on a decision is OPEN only when (1) the last status line is `ANSWERED BY THE OWNER`, or (2) the last status line is `RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION` **and** the last check line is `not required`, `confirmed` or `confirmed with corrections applied`. Every other state is CLOSED, including no status line at all, `pending`, a withdrawn resolution and a referral. **A task whose text requires the owner's own words** (for example the mobility split, T-102) **is open only 

```
gate(){ s=$(grep -F "$1 STATUS:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1); c=$(grep -F "$1 CHECK:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1); case "$s" in *"ANSWERED BY THE OWNER"*) echo "$1 OPEN (owner)";; *"RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION"*) case "$c" in *"not required"*|*confirmed*) echo "$1 OPEN (delegated; ${c#*CHECK: })";; *) echo "$1 CLOSED (check: ${c:-none})";; esac;; *) echo "$1 CLOSED (${s:-no status line})";; esac; }
```

**What it replaces.** The `grep -n -F "OD-NN:"` checks in the task files, which a delegated line, a withdrawn line and an owner's answer all satisfied alike. The `OD-NN:` answer lines stay as the record of what was answered; they no longer open a gate by themselves.

CONDITION: any task or session deciding whether a register decision is settled enough to act on.
ACTION: (1) Run the gate above for each decision the task names; act only on OPEN. (2) For a task that requires the owner's words, act only on `ANSWERED BY THE OWNER`. (3) When recording an owner's answer to a register decision, add the line `OD-NN STATUS: ANSWERED BY THE OWNER` in the same entry. (4) Never edit a status or check line; append a new one.
DATE: 2026-11-12 — convention recorded in the delegated pass, not an owner statement.
